decisions.decision: App is strictly on-device: no accounts, no network calls of any kind, no third-party SDKs (including analytics/crash reporting), and no iCloud/CloudKit sync of SwiftData unless the user explicitly requests it later.
decisions.rationale: Prompt mandates fully offline, no third-party SDKs; iCloud sync and analytics SDKs are easy to accidentally introduce via SwiftData/Xcode defaults and would silently violate that.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing default SwiftData+CloudKit mirroring since it's 'first-party'
constraints: No network traffic verifiable via network conditioner
No third-party dependency in the dependency graph

decisions.decision: Native stack locked to SwiftUI, SwiftData, Core Image/Metal, Swift Charts, StoreKit 2, targeting iOS 17+.
decisions.rationale: Matches prompt's explicit stack mandate and factory rules default to SwiftUI-first, no third-party packages.
constraints: iOS 17+ minimum target

decisions.decision: Visual quality of the generative card is a hard gate enforced via an explicit visual-review checkpoint (rendered output judged across 8-10+ seed/mood/chip combinations), not merely 'it renders without crashing.'
decisions.rationale: Standard build gates (compiles, unit tests, simulator boot) cannot detect 'looks like a gradient-picker demo'; the prompt states beauty is the single most important requirement.
rejected_alternatives: Treating render-success as sufficient proof of visual quality
constraints: Later build/verification phases must produce and inspect rendered output at multiple combinations before declaring the card engine done

decisions.decision: The generative engine must be deterministic per (date seed + mood + chips): identical inputs on the same day always render an identical card; different days/inputs must render meaningfully different compositions, not palette recolors of one template.
decisions.rationale: Prompt explicitly requires this as the technical heart of the app, with the same rigor as an algorithm module.
constraints: Documented seed-space mapping required
Verifiable via repeated runs and cross-combination comparison

decisions.decision: Paid 'regenerate once per day' feature must use an additional seed dimension (a nonce/counter) layered on top of the base date+mood+chips seed, rather than re-running the same deterministic seed.
decisions.rationale: As written, determinism and regeneration are in direct conflict — regenerating with the exact same seed would be a functional no-op and a real bug, only caught if someone actually taps the button and compares output.
rejected_alternatives: Applying strict same-inputs-same-output determinism to the post-regeneration state as well
constraints: Base-card determinism guarantee applies only pre-regeneration
Regenerated card must be visibly different from the original for identical date/mood/chips

decisions.decision: Daily lock is keyed to device local calendar day and must explicitly handle DST transitions, timezone travel, and backward manual clock changes without producing duplicate or skipped days; a backward clock change must never re-unlock an already-completed day.
decisions.rationale: Prompt calls for correct timezone/DST handling but doesn't spell out the backward-clock edge case, which is a common source of real date-boundary bugs.
rejected_alternatives: Treating 'handle timezone/DST' as satisfied without a concrete test for backward clock changes
constraints: Needs a concrete testable definition of which calendar/timezone snapshot governs lock state

decisions.decision: Demo history (30+ seeded days) must be clearly labeled as demo data, and toggling it off (or the user beginning real check-ins) must not silently blend fabricated days into the real streak/stats.
decisions.rationale: Factory rules forbid presenting placeholder/sample data as real; demo mode is for first-review non-emptiness only.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing demo days to silently count toward real streak by default
constraints: Demo mode must be an explicit, visibly labeled state

decisions.decision: StoreKit/IAP verification claims are capped honestly: Simulator can confirm purchase initiation and the local StoreKit configuration's product listing/restore logic, but never full real transaction completion — later phases must state this explicitly rather than claiming full verification.
decisions.rationale: Prompt explicitly demands not faking purchase success and acknowledges Simulator's real limitation.
rejected_alternatives: Claiming IAP fully verified based on Simulator testing alone
constraints: Restore-purchases must have a defined, honest 'nothing to restore' state, not a silent no-op or crash

decisions.decision: Static high-resolution 1080x1920 image export is the hard share-export requirement; a short looping video/Live Photo-style clip is a stretch goal that must never block completion.
decisions.rationale: The prompt itself marks video export as 'ideally,' and video/Metal/AVFoundation encoding is a genuinely hard problem that could sink the build if treated as mandatory.
rejected_alternatives: Treating video export as an equally hard requirement alongside static image export
constraints: Exported image must be verifiably not a raw UI screenshot (no chrome, correct pixel dimensions)

decisions.decision: Free-tier exports carry a small, dismissible-only-via-purchase watermark that must never obscure the card's visual center or caption; Aura+ removes it.
decisions.rationale: Prompt requires the watermark be tasteful and non-intrusive enough to preserve shareability while still being a real monetization hook.
constraints: Watermark placement must not cover focal art or caption text

decisions.decision: Aura is positioned as a daily-ritual-plus-collectible-art product (closest pattern: Co-Star/tarot-style daily card pull + Spotify Wrapped-style monthly recap), not a data-first mood tracker like Daylio.
decisions.rationale: The value proposition is receiving/owning a beautiful deterministic daily artifact, not logging data; this framing should drive UX tone and priority (ceremony and art quality over data density).
rejected_alternatives: Framing Aura primarily as a mood-tracking/journaling app with generative art as a bonus feature
constraints: Audience and comparable-apps claims are ASSUMPTION, pattern-matched from general knowledge, not fetched research

decisions.decision: Rendered cards must be generated once and persisted as an actual image (plus recipe/parameters) at generation time; the widget, archive thumbnails, and export pipeline must all read this cached render rather than re-invoking the generative engine live.
decisions.rationale: WidgetKit timelines run under tight CPU/memory/time budgets and cannot reliably re-run a CIFilter chain or custom Metal shader live; re-deriving on each view also risks non-determinism if any input (e.g. time-of-day) changes between renders.
rejected_alternatives: Re-running the generative engine live inside the widget or on each archive/export view
constraints: Widget, archive, and export must share one persisted rendered artifact per card, not independently regenerate it

decisions.decision: If time-of-day is used as part of the seed, it must be resolved and frozen at the moment of card generation, and never recomputed when the card is viewed later (archive, widget, export).
decisions.rationale: Recomputing a time-of-day-dependent seed live would break the determinism guarantee already established in prompt_contract — a past card could render differently depending on when it's viewed.
rejected_alternatives: Recomputing seed inputs live on each render for simplicity
constraints: Seed resolution must happen exactly once per card, at generation time

decisions.decision: Simulator-only visual review is explicitly acknowledged as not equivalent to on-device Metal/Core Image review, due to potential color space and GPU family differences; this limitation must be stated honestly rather than treated as sufficient verification.
decisions.rationale: The visual-review checkpoint already required by prompt_contract could be silently satisfied by Simulator screenshots alone, which don't guarantee on-device visual fidelity.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Simulator visual review as fully equivalent to on-device review
constraints: Any later claim of 'visual review complete' must note whether it was Simulator-only or on-device

decisions.decision: v1 scope is: deterministic engine + one genuinely beautiful renderer, check-in flow, SwiftData persistence, 30+ day labeled demo history, and end-to-end static 1080x1920 image export. Widget, notifications, and animated Wrapped variants are secondary/dependent; video/Live Photo export is fully out of scope for v1 (not attempted-then-abandoned).
decisions.rationale: Smallest defensible v1 that satisfies the prompt's stated priority order (beauty > determinism > export); avoids sinking build time on Metal/AVFoundation video encoding at the expense of the actually-graded requirement (card beauty).
rejected_alternatives: Attempting video/Live Photo export as an equal-priority v1 feature
constraints: Video/Live Photo export must not be started at the expense of core engine polish or static export correctness

decisions.decision: Aura is built as a single iOS app project (slug: aura); no portfolio split, no sibling projects, no portfolio-json manifest.
decisions.rationale: The prompt requests exactly one app, and the app's systems (check-in, deterministic seed engine, persistence, streaks/trends, monthly Wrapped, export) are tightly interdependent — splitting them would fragment one continuous user experience and one shared state model for no benefit.
rejected_alternatives: Separate apps for check-in/gallery/monetization
Splitting the widget or Wrapped export into its own deliverable for architectural cleanliness
An 'Aura Lite' or companion Watch/onboarding-only app shell
constraints: One app, one bundle identity, one StoreKit non-consumable inside that same app
Widget and share-export stay as extensions of the single target already scoped in prompt_contract, not separate projects

decisions.decision: The build's real failure mode to guard against is a technically-compliant app that reads as a generic SwiftUI gradient exercise, not a missing-feature checklist item — later build/verify phases must judge against this framing explicitly.
decisions.rationale: Per prior phases, beauty is the single most important requirement and is not caught by standard build gates; naming the failure mode concretely at the last pre-implementation checkpoint makes it harder to rubber-stamp later.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'beauty' as an abstract requirement without a concrete failure-mode description to check against
constraints: First-time user reaches a rendered card in under 10 seconds of active interaction, no forced tutorial screens
Archive/trend views must feel alive (not empty-state-as-feature) once demo/seeded history is present
A cold-open share export must look postable, not like a placeholder gradient

decisions.decision: Product promise locked: Aura turns a ten-second daily mood check-in into one deterministic, beautiful generative-art card the user collects, tracks, and shares, entirely on-device with no account/network.
decisions.rationale: Synthesizes the prompt and all upstream decisions into a single testable promise a developer could explain in one sentence.
rejected_alternatives: Framing as a mood-logging/journaling tool with art as a bonus
constraints: Primary user is an aesthetic-minded person with an existing small daily ritual, interacting one-thumb, half-asleep, at a predictable daily moment

decisions.decision: Navigation is four destinations — Today, Archive, Wrapped, Settings — with mood/streak trend views nested as a segmented control inside Archive rather than a separate tab.
decisions.rationale: Trends are naturally 'archive, summarized' rather than an independently-reached destination; five-plus tabs would read as feature-padding on an app this size.
rejected_alternatives: A separate Trends/Stats tab
constraints: Today screen must support three explicit states: not-yet-checked-in, checked-in-and-revealed, and widget-tap deep link

decisions.decision: Tapping the 'your Aura is waiting' widget state must deep-link directly into the check-in flow, not merely foreground the app to a screen requiring a further tap.
decisions.rationale: This is a real lever on the sub-10-second time-to-first-card promise and is an information-architecture decision, not later polish.
rejected_alternatives: Widget tap simply opens the app to its default screen
constraints: Must be implemented as part of the widget/deep-link wiring, not deferred

decisions.decision: Check-in is non-committing until its final step: a force-quit mid-flow with a partial mood/chip pick does not count as 'in progress' against the daily lock, and simply restarts on relaunch.
decisions.rationale: Prevents a crash or force-quit from corrupting daily-lock state or stranding a user in a half-completed day.
rejected_alternatives: Persisting partial check-in state as binding progress toward the day's lock
constraints: Pre-filling the last partial pick on restart is optional (nice-to-have), not required

decisions.decision: A genuine fresh install defaults to a real, well-designed empty state, not demo history turned on by default; demo mode is explicit opt-in and stays visibly labeled the entire time it is active.
decisions.rationale: Reinforces and operationalizes the earlier demo-history labeling decision (DEC-prompt_contract-007) at the product-promise level — a real user's first launch should never be silently populated with fabricated days.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping with demo mode on by default so the app never looks empty out of the box
constraints: Demo mode toggle must be discoverable but not pre-enabled for real installs

decisions.decision: Additional hard scope boundaries for this phase: no social layer (no feed/comments/following), no editing or undoing a locked day's check-in, at most one canonical card per calendar day (regeneration replaces rather than adds an entry), and no cross-device/reinstall data-continuity promise.
decisions.rationale: These are private-object, single-record-per-day guarantees implied by the app's ritual framing and the no-iCloud-sync decision, but not yet explicitly stated as boundaries until now.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing a social/sharing feed of other users' cards
Allowing edits to a locked day's card
Treating a paid regeneration as a second archive entry for the same day
constraints: Archive/streak logic must treat regeneration as a replace-in-place operation, never an additional record

decisions.decision: The exact size of the mood/chip vocabulary and the resulting seed-space dimensionality is explicitly deferred to the generative-algorithm design phase, not decided here.
decisions.rationale: That is an implementation/architecture decision about the seed engine, not a product-promise-level decision this phase should settle by accident.
rejected_alternatives: Pre-specifying an exact mood/chip count now
constraints: Downstream algorithm-design phase owns this decision

decisions.decision: Aura+ (one non-consumable purchase) bundles exactly three functional unlocks: watermark-free exports, an expanded palette library, and one regeneration per day — not cosmetic-only value.
decisions.rationale: A non-consumable unlock still has to keep paying off daily or it reads as a one-time toggle nobody remembers buying; three concrete utility levers make the purchase durable.
rejected_alternatives: Cosmetic-only unlock (e.g. just watermark removal)
Converting Aura+ to a recurring subscription
constraints: Purchase remains a single non-consumable IAP per DEC-prompt_contract-002/010

decisions.decision: Regenerated cards must differ from the original in at least two of {palette, shape-field topology, particle/line density} for identical date/mood/chip inputs.
decisions.rationale: A regeneration that reads as a minor recolor breaks the paid feature's emotional promise even if it is technically a distinct render; this is the concrete, testable acceptance bar.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'visibly different' undefined and trusting subjective judgment at review time
constraints: Verified by regenerating the same mood/chip pair across multiple days in testing and comparing composition, not just hue

decisions.decision: Target user is narrowed to ~16-34, someone who already runs an adjacent small daily self-care/mood app and checks in during dead-time pockets of their day (coffee, before bed).
decisions.rationale: Design decisions (check-in speed, tone, lack of onboarding) need a specific persona, not a broad demographic; this persona's tolerance for friction is near zero.
rejected_alternatives: Broader/generic 'mobile user interested in wellness' framing
constraints: Check-in speed is treated as a retention feature, not a nice-to-have, per documented mood-app novelty-dropoff risk

decisions.decision: An on-demand 'so far this month' mini-recap, reusing the Wrapped rendering pipeline at smaller scope, unlocks once a user has 5-7+ real cards banked, rather than waiting for month-end.
decisions.rationale: A genuine new user otherwise gets zero shareable moments for up to 30 days, exactly the window where they decide whether the app earns a permanent home-screen slot — a real gap in the growth mechanism, not a hypothetical.
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on month-end Wrapped as the only viral/recap surface
constraints: Must reuse the same static composite export pipeline as Wrapped — does not require or imply video/Live Photo export, which remains out of scope

decisions.decision: Build must explicitly audit the SwiftData ModelContainer configuration for cloudKitDatabase: .none (or equivalent) as a concrete guardrail against accidental default CloudKit sync.
decisions.rationale: Several SwiftData project templates default to CloudKit-backed containers; this would silently violate the no-network/no-cloud-dependency requirement already locked in prompt_contract.
rejected_alternatives: Trusting that 'no accounts, no network' as a stated principle is sufficient without a concrete build-time check
constraints: Future v-next cloud sync must be user-opted-in via its own explicit consent screen, never enabled by default container behavior

decisions.decision: Competitive wedge is stated explicitly: Aura is an object-to-own product (deterministic collectible generative artifact), not a data-to-log mood tracker; trend/chart views are a secondary byproduct of collection, not the primary payoff.
decisions.rationale: This is the actual differentiation versus Daylio/How We Feel/Co-Star, who are optimized for insight-over-time with charts as the payoff — naming it concretely should drive UI/tone priority (ceremony over data density) through design and build phases.
rejected_alternatives: Framing Aura as a prettier mood-tracking/analytics app
constraints: Design phases should prioritize the reveal moment and collection feel over dashboard/analytics polish

decisions.decision: Demo-seeded history and freshly-generated cards from equivalent inputs must be visually indistinguishable in rendering quality — distinguishable only by an explicit demo label, never by a quality gap in either direction.
decisions.rationale: If demo data looks better than real output, users sense they're being shown a mockup; if it looks worse, the archive/collection format fails to sell itself during evaluation.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing demo cards to use a higher-effort curated rendering path distinct from the real generative engine
constraints: Acceptance check: 10 demo cards vs. 10 fresh cards from the same mood/chip inputs, side by side, distinguishable only by the demo label

decisions.decision: The daily lock's timezone/DST rule is concretely defined as keying off the last-completed calendar day in the timezone active at the moment of completion, not a naive 'did the wall clock cross midnight' check.
decisions.rationale: This is the exact rule needed to satisfy DEC-prompt_contract-006 without ambiguity, and is the first bug a reviewer finds by changing the Simulator's date/timezone.
rejected_alternatives: Any check based on current wall-clock time alone without recording the timezone context at completion
constraints: Must be verified in build/test by literally changing Simulator date and timezone, not just documented as intent

decisions.decision: MVP slice is the full check-in-to-reveal-to-persist loop plus a populated archive grid and one working static share export; Wrapped, widget, notifications, trend charts, and functional StoreKit purchase/restore/regeneration logic are deferred to the next build slice.
decisions.rationale: Proves the core promise end-to-end (deterministic beautiful card, collected, shareable) without the secondary surfaces that are additive polish on top of a working engine.
rejected_alternatives: A thinner slice that only proves rendering without persistence/archive/export
Including Wrapped/widget/notifications/StoreKit in the first slice
constraints: Later build phase must not treat this slice as needing further product debate before implementation

decisions.decision: 30+ day labeled demo history stays IN this MVP slice rather than being cut, correcting this round's Codex-fallback proposal which had listed it as cuttable.
decisions.rationale: Already locked upstream in DEC-product_research-005 and DEC-prompt_contract-007 as a v1 must-have; without seeded variety across the seed space, the slice cannot actually validate that adjacent days look meaningfully different, which is the core technical claim of the app.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring demo history to a later slice and validating variety with only a handful of manually-generated cards
constraints: Demo history must remain visibly labeled and never silently blend into real streak/stats, per DEC-prompt_contract-007

decisions.decision: One working static 1080x1920 share export with watermark stays IN this MVP slice rather than being cut.
decisions.rationale: Export correctness is explicitly priority (c) in prompt_contract, not a stretch item; validating it only after other features are built risks discovering export/watermark placement problems late.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring export entirely to a later slice
constraints: Full StoreKit purchase logic to remove the watermark is still deferred; only the export pipeline itself and a stubbed/honest paywall affordance are in scope now

decisions.decision: The haptic + spring reveal ceremony is a non-negotiable, load-bearing part of the slice and must not be stubbed or skipped under time pressure.
decisions.rationale: Per phase rules ('keep the slice emotionally satisfying, not just technically minimal') and prior phases' framing of Aura as an object-to-receive, not a data-plumbing demo.
rejected_alternatives: Shipping an instant, unanimated card reveal to save build time
constraints: If something must be cut under time pressure, it must not be this

decisions.decision: Validation criteria for this slice are: sub-10-second cold-launch-to-revealed-card with no forced tutorial; byte-identical same-day-same-input renders; visually distinct output across 8-10+ combinations (human-eyeballed, not just unit-tested); force-quit non-committing; Simulator date/timezone changes produce no duplicate/skipped day; demo cards visually indistinguishable from real ones except for label; exported image has correct dimensions, no UI chrome, and non-overlapping watermark.
decisions.rationale: Operationalizes the success bars already stated across prior phases into one concrete checklist the build phase can be held to.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving validation as general prose without a checkable list
constraints: These checks must be exercised by literally regenerating/manipulating Simulator state, not just documented as intent

decisions.decision: Caption selection must enforce a no-repeat window (captions not reused within the trailing 30 days for a given mood), with the phrase bank sized to make this achievable.
decisions.rationale: Text repetition is far more noticeable to a user than compositional art variation, and a small bank would surface repeats within weeks of daily use, undermining the 'never feels templated' promise.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving caption bank sizing/repetition unaddressed and discovering collisions only through real usage
constraints: Deterministic selection must still be reproducible per day, drawing only from the eligible (non-recently-used) subset

decisions.decision: The regeneration credit and the daily lock must be tracked from one shared canonical 'last completed calendar day' state, not two independent date checks.
decisions.rationale: If regeneration uses its own naive date comparison, rolling the device clock back and forward grants unlimited free regenerations, breaking the one-per-day paid feature's premise even though the daily-lock backward-clock rule (DEC-prompt_contract-006) was already satisfied.
rejected_alternatives: Tracking regeneration eligibility with a separate 'used today: bool' reset on its own date comparison
constraints: Build phase must implement both the daily lock and regeneration credit against the same state source

decisions.decision: The app must explicitly trigger a WidgetKit timeline reload as part of the check-in completion path, not rely on WidgetKit picking up the new card unassisted.
decisions.rationale: WidgetKit doesn't know a new card exists unless told; a missed or delayed reload leaves the widget showing 'your Aura is waiting' after the user already checked in, directly undermining the widget's role as the durable retention channel identified in product_research.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming WidgetKit's normal timeline refresh cadence is sufficient
constraints: Must be a testable, explicit step in the check-in completion code path

decisions.decision: Pending local daily-reminder notifications must be cancelled/rescheduled immediately on successful check-in; notification permission is requested contextually (after first completed check-in or via Settings), never at first launch; a denied permission gets a deep link back to Settings.app.
decisions.rationale: An uncancelled reminder for an already-completed check-in erodes trust in a ritual app; requesting permission at first launch tanks opt-in and violates HIG guidance; a denied permission needs a real path back in rather than a dead end.
rejected_alternatives: Requesting notification permission at first app launch
Leaving scheduled notifications unmanaged after check-in completes
constraints: Cancellation must be part of the check-in completion transaction, not a best-effort background step

decisions.decision: Demo history occupies a fixed historical date range strictly before install/first real check-in (collision with real check-in dates is structurally impossible), and disabling demo mode shows an explicit confirmation that the streak will reset to real check-ins only.
decisions.rationale: Runtime conflict resolution between demo and real days on the same date is a bug surface that shouldn't exist; a silent streak-number drop when toggling demo mode off reads as an app bug rather than expected behavior.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing demo history to keep generating forward while enabled, requiring runtime date-collision handling
Silently changing the displayed streak count when demo mode is toggled off
constraints: Demo date range must be computed once, anchored before real usage begins

decisions.decision: StoreKit entitlement state must be kept current via a live Transaction.updates listener, not only a one-time check at launch; this is documented as its own honest verification gap separate from Simulator's inability to complete real transactions.
decisions.rationale: Without a live listener, a refund or a restore on another path won't reflect in the app until the next cold launch, which is invisible to Simulator-only testing and could let a refunded user keep premium features for a session.
rejected_alternatives: Checking Transaction.currentEntitlements only once at app launch
constraints: Honesty disclaimer for StoreKit verification must name this gap distinctly from DEC-prompt_contract-008's transaction-completion caveat

decisions.decision: A SwiftData store load failure (corruption, disk full, future migration failure) must be detected and surfaced as an explicit error state, never silently treated as a fresh empty store.
decisions.rationale: The entire product value is the accumulated card collection; silently starting a user over with zero cards on a load failure is a direct betrayal of the 'archive worth protecting' promise.
rejected_alternatives: Letting a failed store load fall through to an empty-state UI indistinguishable from a genuine fresh install
constraints: Error state must be distinguishable from the genuine empty-state (new user) UI

decisions.decision: Card accessibility descriptions are generated from mood/chip/caption metadata (e.g. 'a warm, calm morning aura'), not attempted visual/pixel description; mood/chip pickers must be distinguishable by non-color means (shape/icon/label) for color-blind users.
decisions.rationale: VoiceOver cannot meaningfully describe an abstract generative composition, and an entirely palette-organized picker UI is unusable for color-blind users without a non-color differentiator.
rejected_alternatives: Omitting meaningful accessibility descriptions for generative cards
Relying on color alone to distinguish mood/chip options
constraints: Applies to card detail views, archive grid, and widget

decisions.decision: Exported images must not leak EXIF/device metadata, and the watermark asset must be fully bundled in the app, never fetched remotely.
decisions.rationale: A remotely-fetched watermark asset would be a network call at the exact moment of sharing, violating the no-network requirement; metadata leakage is a privacy concern for a supposedly private, on-device app.
rejected_alternatives: Fetching or updating the watermark asset remotely for easier iteration
constraints: Applies to both per-card export and Wrapped export

decisions.decision: The 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (DEC-prompt_contract-003) is explicitly blocked on the mood/chip vocabulary being fixed by the algorithm-design phase; that phase owns unblocking it, not just picking a vocabulary size in isolation.
decisions.rationale: There is no defined sample universe for the visual-review checkpoint until the vocabulary size is fixed, so the dependency needs to be named explicitly rather than assumed to resolve itself.
rejected_alternatives: Treating vocabulary-size deferral (DEC-initial_discussion-007) as unrelated to the visual-review checkpoint's readiness
constraints: Algorithm-design phase must treat 'unblocks visual-review checkpoint' as part of its deliverable, not a side effect

decisions.decision: Entitlement changes (e.g. purchasing Aura+ mid-day) must never retroactively mutate an already-persisted card's render; only cards generated after the purchase, plus a spent regeneration credit, may reflect the new entitlement.
decisions.rationale: Preserves the render-once-persist-forever architecture (DEC-product_research-002) and the core determinism guarantee; computing the active palette set live from current entitlement would let the same (date+mood+chips) seed produce different output depending purely on purchase timing.
rejected_alternatives: Computing the active palette/entitlement set live at render or view time instead of snapshotting it
constraints: Entitlement state used for rendering must be snapshotted and stored with the card record at generation time, same as other seed inputs

decisions.decision: The international date-line / transoceanic travel edge case is resolved explicitly as 'local calendar day wins,' accepting that this can legitimately produce two check-ins within under 24 real-world hours (eastward travel) or an apparent one-day streak gap (westward travel) for a traveler who did nothing wrong.
decisions.rationale: This is a materially different case from the already-solved DST/backward-clock cheating scenario; avoids over-engineering a vanishingly rare edge case with elapsed-real-time tracking, which would also risk destabilizing the already-correct simpler rule.
rejected_alternatives: Tracking elapsed real-world hours between check-ins to prevent double-checkin or apparent gaps from transoceanic travel
constraints: This is a named, accepted limitation, not a bug — must not motivate later ad hoc complexity that risks breaking the DST/backward-clock rule

decisions.decision: The WidgetKit timeline reload trigger (DEC-detailed_discussion-003) must fire on both check-in completion and successful regeneration, as two distinct call sites.
decisions.rationale: A regenerated card is a second point where the persisted render changes; without its own explicit reload trigger, the widget shows a stale pre-regeneration card exactly like the original check-in-completion bug it was meant to fix.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming the check-in-completion reload trigger also covers regeneration
constraints: Must be implemented and tested as two separate trigger points in code, not one shared assumption

decisions.decision: The restore-purchases success confirmation must explicitly state that card history/streak stays device-local and is not restored or backed up, distinct from the entitlement itself which is restored.
decisions.rationale: Combines two already-locked boundaries (no cross-device/reinstall continuity, and an honest restore-purchases success state) that collide into a real support/perception gap: a reinstall+restore correctly returns Aura+ but leaves an empty archive, which reads as data loss next to a bare 'restored!' banner.
rejected_alternatives: A generic 'purchase restored' confirmation with no mention of local-only history
constraints: Applies specifically to the restore-purchases success path, distinct from DEC-prompt_contract-008's honest 'nothing to restore' state

decisions.decision: Full feature set is prioritized must/should/could/won't rather than treating the prompt's eight feature bullets as eight equal must-haves.
decisions.rationale: Some prompt features (widget, notifications, Wrapped, trend charts) are explicitly secondary/dependent per upstream product_research and per_app_product_brief decisions; restating all eight as equal musts would misrepresent already-settled prioritization.
rejected_alternatives: Treating every one of the prompt's eight numbered features as an equal must-have
constraints: requirements-json core:true set maps to must-have; core:false maps to should/could/guardrail

decisions.decision: Full StoreKit 2 wiring (purchase, restore, live entitlement listener, regeneration-entitlement rules) stays a must-have for this full build, but is explicitly flagged as the single riskiest must-have; if scope must be trimmed under time pressure, trim within StoreKit's three unlocks (e.g. ship watermark removal + one regeneration correctly, treat expanded palette themes as could) rather than rushing the core engine or export pipeline.
decisions.rationale: StoreKit is explicitly core to the prompt and this phase scopes the full build (not another MVP slice), but it is also the item where 'what's implemented' and 'what Simulator can prove' diverge most, and where the four already-locked entitlement rules are easiest to silently violate under time pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Demoting StoreKit to should/could to reduce risk
Treating StoreKit as equally low-risk as the rest of the must-have list
constraints: If cut, cut inside StoreKit's own three unlocks, never by rushing the generative engine or export pipeline

decisions.decision: Widget and local notifications are scored as should-have, not must-have, for this build.
decisions.rationale: Both are real retention value but are second surfaces layered on an already-working render pipeline, and were already explicitly deferred once in next_steps_small for the same reason; a locked IA/behavior decision (e.g. widget deep-link, dual reload triggers) governs how they're built if built, but doesn't promote their priority.
rejected_alternatives: Treating widget/notifications as must-haves because they were both in the original prompt's numbered feature list
constraints: If built, must still follow the already-locked widget-deep-link and dual-reload-trigger rules from initial_discussion and detailed_discussion

decisions.decision: Monthly Wrapped, the on-demand mini-recap, and the mood-distribution trend view are scored as should-have, not must-have.
decisions.rationale: Consistent with product_research calling Wrapped 'secondary/dependent' and per_app_product_brief framing trend/chart views as a byproduct of collection rather than the payoff.
rejected_alternatives: Promoting Wrapped to must-have given the prompt calls it a primary viral surface
constraints: Trend view stays nested inside Archive per DEC-initial_discussion-002 if built; mini-recap reuses the Wrapped static pipeline per DEC-per_app_product_brief-004 if built

decisions.decision: Could-list is defined as: additional palette themes beyond the Aura+ baseline, a richer caption bank beyond the 30-day no-repeat minimum, additional widget size variants, onboarding polish beyond the zero-tutorial requirement, and accessibility refinements beyond the metadata-description baseline.
decisions.rationale: None of these block the core product promise if cut; they are enhancements on top of already-must-have baselines.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the could-list undefined and deciding ad hoc during build
constraints: Could-items must not be built at the expense of any must-have

decisions.decision: Won't-build list is restated explicitly as this phase's contract: no social/feed layer, no editing/undoing a locked day, no second archive record for regeneration, no cross-device/iCloud sync or reinstall continuity, no video/Live Photo export, no analytics/crash SDKs, no third-party dependencies.
decisions.rationale: These were already decided in principle across earlier phases; restating them here makes them part of this phase's explicit machine-readable contract rather than only implied by earlier prose.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving these boundaries implicit rather than restated in this phase's own output
constraints: Later build/verify phases check the built app against this list as explicit non-goals, not just must-haves

decisions.decision: Every acceptance criterion in the requirements-json contract must be phrased as a concrete, reviewer-executable action (e.g. 'change the Simulator's date/timezone and confirm no duplicate/skipped day') rather than a vague adjective (e.g. 'handles timezone correctly').
decisions.rationale: Vague acceptance criteria are exactly how a technically-compliant, visually-mediocre build passes the gate — the failure mode portfolio_selection already named as the one to guard against.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing prose-level acceptance criteria without concrete reviewer actions
constraints: Later build/verify phases must be graded against the concrete phrasing in requirements-json, not a looser restatement

decisions.decision: App design language is named 'Dusk Gallery': dark-first, low-contrast chrome, translucent frosted surfaces letting each card's palette bleed into surrounding UI, generous negative space, motion on slow physical springs.
decisions.rationale: The persona checks in half-asleep or pre-bed; the chrome must recede so the generative card reads as the one considered object on screen, like a piece in an underlit gallery room, distinct from what a productivity or logging app would want.
rejected_alternatives: Generic 'clean and modern' styling with no named rationale
constraints: Applies to all screens: Today, Archive, Wrapped, Settings

decisions.decision: Emotional target is locked: the user should feel like something was quietly made for them today, worth a few seconds of attention — anticipation resolving into specific delight, never gamified urgency or clinical logging.
decisions.rationale: Gives later phases a concrete bar for tone in copy, animation pacing, and interaction design.

decisions.decision: Signature interaction is the live bloom reveal: after the final chip tap, the actual Core Image/Metal generative pipeline renders on-screen over ~1.5-2s with three distinct haptic beats (light/medium/heavy-confirm), caption fading in half a beat after the art settles.
decisions.rationale: The app's premise ('made for you today') depends on the reveal visibly being the real engine constructing output live, not a canned animation over a pre-rendered static image.
rejected_alternatives: Instant pop-in of the finished card
A generic push/fade transition to a static image
Pre-rendering the animation separately from the actual generative output
constraints: Reveal must invoke the real rendering pipeline, not a decorative animation layered on top of an already-finished image

decisions.decision: The stock/default UI approach (system List rows for archive, segmented Picker for mood, generic share-sheet screenshot, UIKit alert for purchase, default large-title NavigationStack chrome) is explicitly rejected in favor of: a custom palette-tinted grid for archive, a cluster of tactile icon+label shapes for mood/chip selection, the live bloom reveal, and a minimal custom top bar with no default large-title box.
decisions.rationale: Each default pattern actively undermines the collection/ritual framing (list reads as data, segmented control reads as settings, large-title box creates a visible seam in dark mode) or fails accessibility (color-only mood/chip differentiation excludes colorblind users).
rejected_alternatives: Using default SwiftUI List/Picker/NavigationStack chrome for speed of implementation
constraints: Build phase must implement custom grid, custom picker shapes, and custom top bar rather than stock components

decisions.decision: Today screen has six distinct states: cold-launch skeleton, not-yet-checked-in (dim unlit aura silhouette), check-in steps (mood then chip, time-of-day resolved silently), bloom reveal, settled revealed state (with regeneration visibly gated, not hidden, for free users), and a store-load-failure error state visually and textually distinct from the genuine new-user empty state.
decisions.rationale: Conflating a store-load failure with a genuine empty state would silently read as data loss, the exact failure mode already warned against upstream; showing free users a visibly-gated (not hidden) regenerate affordance surfaces the paid feature as a real upsell rather than an invisible one.
rejected_alternatives: Treating store-load failure and new-user-empty as the same UI state
Hiding the regenerate affordance entirely for free-tier users
constraints: Widget tap must deep-link to whichever of these six states is currently true, not just foreground the app to a default screen

decisions.decision: Archive grid cells carry the demo-history badge directly on the cell itself, in addition to a dismissible top banner while demo mode is active; a genuine empty state is a designed icon+line+CTA, never bare 'no cards yet' text.
decisions.rationale: Banners get scrolled past; the grid must remain self-explanatory about demo-vs-real status even after a user forgets the banner exists, per the already-locked demo-labeling requirement.
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on a top banner to indicate demo mode is active
constraints: Applies per-cell in the archive grid, not just at the screen level

decisions.decision: Wrapped shows an explicit 'not yet unlocked, check in a few more days' state before the first month boundary or mini-recap threshold is reached, rather than appearing empty or broken.
decisions.rationale: Wrapped is one of four named nav destinations; a dormant-looking tab reads as a bug rather than a feature that hasn't unlocked yet.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the Wrapped tab in a generic empty state indistinguishable from a broken screen
constraints: Applies until either the first calendar month boundary or the 5-7+ card mini-recap threshold is met

decisions.decision: Caption text over generative art requires a defined legibility treatment (scrim, frosted text plate, or adaptive text color sampled from the underlying art), and the bloom reveal requires an explicit Reduce Motion fallback (a gentler crossfade preserving the same haptic beats), decided now rather than left to build-time discovery.
decisions.rationale: Caption legibility against an arbitrary busy composition and Reduce Motion support for the app's single signature moment are both concrete failure risks that a generic 'add accessibility later' approach would miss.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving caption contrast unaddressed until a real collision is found in testing
Simply disabling the bloom animation for Reduce Motion with no alternate reveal
constraints: Reduce Motion fallback must preserve the same haptic beats as the full bloom, only removing the physical motion

decisions.decision: A single @MainActor @Observable AuraStore, injected via environment, is the sole owner of the canonical last-completed-calendar-day value, entitlement snapshot, and demo-mode state; no view or screen independently queries SwiftData to compute its own notion of 'today' or entitlement.
decisions.rationale: The daily-lock/regeneration-credit shared-day-state rule (DEC-detailed_discussion-002) and entitlement-snapshotting rule (DEC-detailed_discussion-011) are only actually shared if there is one source of truth in code; scattered per-view @Query-based date/entitlement checks are exactly how those two rules would silently drift apart under a clock change.
rejected_alternatives: Per-screen @Query-based computation of day-state and entitlement
constraints: Build phase must implement one AuraStore instance injected via environment, not per-screen state duplication

decisions.decision: Navigation is a TabView with a fully custom tab bar (not just custom NavigationStack chrome) — stock translucent tab bar material is explicitly rejected because it double-blurs against Dusk Gallery's own frosted surfaces; each tab owns its own NavigationStack driven by a typed route enum (TodayRoute, ArchiveRoute, WrappedRoute), with a single PendingDeepLink value on the store consumed once via .onChange to resolve widget taps into the correct tab + path + Today sub-state.
decisions.rationale: The widget-tap-must-land-on-exact-current-state requirement (DEC-initial_discussion-003, DEC-design_discussion-005) has no concrete implementation path without a programmatic deep-link mechanism external to the view hierarchy; raw NavigationLink(destination:) cannot be pushed into from outside the tree.
rejected_alternatives: Stock translucent tab bar material
Raw NavigationLink(destination:) navigation without a typed route/deep-link mechanism
constraints: Build phase must implement PendingDeepLink + typed route enums, not ad hoc navigation state

decisions.decision: The widget extension requires an App Group shared container holding cached rendered PNGs plus card/palette metadata; the widget reads only this shared cache and never touches the main app's ModelContext directly.
decisions.rationale: This is invisible until the widget target is actually wired up and easy to skip under time pressure since the main app functions fine without it; without it, the widget cannot read the cached-render architecture already mandated by DEC-product_research-002.
rejected_alternatives: Widget reading the app's default sandboxed Documents directory or ModelContext directly
constraints: Must be an explicit line item (app group identifier, shared container URL) in the build handoff

decisions.decision: The bloom reveal's 'real engine, not a decorative animation' requirement is concretely defined as: 4 genuine cached intermediate composites (seed-point/palette wash, shape-field placement, particle/line density pass, final color grade) generated once at render time from the actual filter/shader chain, cross-dissolved along the spring timeline with the three haptic beats aligned to the 1→2, 2→3, and 3→4(settle) transitions.
decisions.rationale: Literally re-stepping the CIFilter/Metal composite graph every display frame in sync with a spring curve would jank on older supported devices; without a concrete definition, 'real engine' either becomes a performance trap or gets quietly faked as a crossfade over one pre-rendered static image, which would be invisible in review.
rejected_alternatives: Re-running the full filter/shader chain live on every display frame
A crossfade/decorative animation layered over a single pre-rendered final image
constraints: Build phase must generate and cache all 4 intermediate composites at generation/regeneration time, verifiable as 4 distinct real artifacts, not 1

decisions.decision: Archive grid uses LazyVGrid with cell identity keyed to each card's canonical date-string ID (never array index), rendering a separately-generated, separately-cached small thumbnail (~400x700) distinct from the full 1080x1920 export artifact.
decisions.rationale: Regeneration replaces a card in place (DEC-initial_discussion-006), so index-keyed identity would show stale content or animate the wrong cell on a regen; loading 30+ full-res exports into a scrolling grid is a real memory risk on older devices, and generating thumbnails at scroll-time would violate the cached-render-only architecture (DEC-product_research-002).
rejected_alternatives: Index-keyed ForEach identity
Rendering full-resolution 1080x1920 images directly in grid cells
Generating thumbnails on-demand at scroll time
constraints: Thumbnail generation must happen once alongside the full-res export, at card generation/regeneration time

decisions.decision: Concrete visual-system values are locked: 8pt spacing base with 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 steps; type scale mapped to Dynamic Type styles (Display 34/40 Bold→.largeTitle for Wrapped poster headline only, Title 22/28 Semibold→.title2 for the custom top bar, Card Caption 20/26 Semibold→.title3, Body 17/22 Regular→.body, Subhead 15/20 Medium→.subheadline, Caption 13/16 Medium→.caption); corner radii small 8 / medium 16 / large 24 / pill 999.
decisions.rationale: The phase playbook requires explicit point values with zero adjectives standing in for numbers so a SwiftUI builder can write Theme.swift directly.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving spacing/type/radius values as adjectives for the build phase to invent
constraints: Color hex values for semantic roles still outstanding — see open_risks

decisions.decision: The caption legibility treatment (DEC-design_discussion-008) is concretely specified as a frosted text plate (12pt corner radius), not a raw drop-shadow, with an automatic fallback rule: if the adaptive/sampled-from-art text color ever computes below 4.5:1 contrast against its background, the UI falls back to the frosted plate automatically rather than relying on every generated composition happening to be legible by construction.
decisions.rationale: A drop-shadow reads cheap against painterly art and fails on light/busy compositions; since composition varies a lot by design, some seed/mood combinations will produce low-contrast adaptive text by construction, so a hoped-for outcome isn't sufficient — a concrete, testable fallback rule is needed.
rejected_alternatives: Raw drop-shadow as the sole legibility treatment
Relying on adaptive sampled color without a guaranteed-contrast fallback
constraints: Fallback trigger (4.5:1 contrast ratio) must be implemented as a real runtime check, not a design assumption

decisions.decision: No external Claude Design handoff is used for this app; the design spec is delivered as code-ready values (spacing, type, radii, component/architecture specs) for a SwiftUI builder to implement directly.
decisions.rationale: The app's entire visual differentiator is the generative engine's rendered output, which no static mockup tool can produce or meaningfully preview; an external design pass risks anchoring effort on decorative chrome polish while the actual gating problem (does the real CIFilter/Metal composition read as beautiful across 8-10+ seed combinations) can only be solved and judged in code against real rendered output.
rejected_alternatives: Producing a Claude Design prompt/upload plan for external mockup of chrome or card templates
constraints: Build/verify phases must judge visual quality against real rendered engine output, not any external mockup

decisions.decision: Semantic color roles are locked with explicit light+dark hex values: Background #0B0B12/#F6F5F8, Surface #17161F/#FFFFFF, SurfaceElevated #1F1E29/#FDFCFF, TextPrimary #F2F1F6/#16151C, TextSecondary #A6A3B3/#5B5868, Accent #B98CFF/#7C4DFF, Success #5FD9A4/#1E9E6E, Warning #FFC773/#B8720A, Error #FF7A7A/#D93A3A, Hairline #2A2836@60%/#E4E2EA, plus a distinct DemoBadge tint (amber #FFD37A on #3A2E12 dark, #8A5A00 on #FFF3DC light).
decisions.rationale: Phase acceptance checks require every color role to have both a light and dark hex value; the demo badge specifically needs its own tint (not Accent) so it reads as a status label rather than an interactive control, which also satisfies the existing non-color-differentiation accessibility rule.
rejected_alternatives: Reusing Accent violet for the demo badge tint
constraints: TextPrimary/TextSecondary pairs must maintain 4.5:1 contrast against their respective Background/Surface pairs in both appearances

decisions.decision: Per-screen empty/error/locked states are specified with concrete copy, icon, and recovery action rather than referenced by name from design_discussion: Today not-yet-checked-in (breathing silhouette + headline/subhead/CTA), store-load-failure (rose triangle icon, 'not lost data' framing, Try Again + Copy Diagnostic Info), Archive empty (gallery-frame icon + CTA to Today), Wrapped locked (dynamic countdown copy picking whichever unlock condition is sooner, plus a secondary link to Today).
decisions.rationale: Cross-referencing an earlier phase's state model by name isn't sufficient for a builder to implement directly; the store-load-failure state in particular needs a support-facing recovery action (Copy Diagnostic Info), since a user told 'your data is inaccessible' with no way to report it is a real support gap.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving per-screen state copy as an implicit cross-reference to design_discussion
constraints: Store-load-failure copy/icon must be visually distinct from any empty state, per DEC-design_discussion-005

decisions.decision: EmptyStateView and ErrorStateView are single shared, parameterized components (icon, headline, subhead, primary action, optional secondary action) reused across Today, Archive, and Wrapped, rather than bespoke per-screen views; Archive's store-load-failure state reuses the exact same ErrorStateView instance/styling as Today's, not a lookalike.
decisions.rationale: Three hand-built near-identical empty/error views are exactly the kind of duplication that drifts out of sync the first time copy changes in one place and not the others; a single underlying store-load failure visible from two tabs should not produce two different-looking error screens, which would itself look like a bug.
rejected_alternatives: Bespoke empty/error view per screen
constraints: Build phase must implement one EmptyStateView and one ErrorStateView component, parameterized per call site, not per-screen duplicates

decisions.decision: Full component inventory locked and mapped to screens (Theme.swift, AuraTabBar, AuraTopBar, AuraSilhouetteView, SkeletonPulseView, MoodChipCluster, WordChipCluster, BloomRevealView, AuraCardView, CaptionPlate, StreakChip, RegenerateButton, ShareButton, ArchiveGrid/ArchiveCell, DemoBadge/DemoModeBanner, EmptyStateView/ErrorStateView, WrappedLockedStateView, AuraPlusCard, RestorePurchasesRow, NotificationSettingsRow, DemoModeToggleRow, ConfirmationSheet, ToastBanner); a Wrapped poster is implemented as AuraCardView at a different aspect/composite treatment, not a separate rendering path.
decisions.rationale: Satisfies the phase's component-inventory acceptance check with no screen left implicit; treating the Wrapped poster as a variant of AuraCardView rather than a new rendering path avoids a second place where the cached-render architecture or beauty bar could be implemented inconsistently.
rejected_alternatives: A wholly separate rendering/component path for Wrapped posters distinct from the per-card AuraCardView
constraints: Build phase must implement exactly this component list; new bespoke views should be justified against this inventory, not added ad hoc

decisions.decision: The round-1 decision to decline external Claude Design handoff (DEC-design_handoff-008) is reaffirmed now that the token/component spec is complete.
decisions.rationale: A complete code-ready spec makes an external static mockup even less valuable, since it would add process without adding information a SwiftUI builder doesn't already have.
rejected_alternatives: Revisiting external design now that more detail exists

decisions.decision: Rendering engine is a single CIFilter-based pipeline (stock filters plus custom CIColorKernel/CIWarpKernel where flow-field/particle math needs more control), rendered through one shared CIContext, reused identically for all 4 bloom intermediates, the full-res 1080x1920 export, the archive/widget thumbnail, and the Wrapped poster — no separate Metal/MTKView live-rendering path.
decisions.rationale: A split Metal-for-reveal / CIFilter-for-export architecture would be two rendering implementations that must stay visually consistent, the same two-sources-of-truth bug shape already flagged elsewhere in this project (day-state, widget reload, entitlement snapshots) — except here it would hit the one thing the whole app is graded on.
rejected_alternatives: Custom Metal/MTKView shader for the live bloom reveal with a separate CIFilter path for static export
constraints: All rendered artifacts (bloom intermediates, export, thumbnail, Wrapped poster) must go through the same CIContext/filter graph

decisions.decision: The determinism contract is split into two layers: a pure, synchronous, Codable/Hashable 'recipe' struct (palette index, shape-field topology params, density values, caption index) computed from (date, mood, chips, entitlement snapshot, regeneration nonce) is the actual same-inputs-same-output guarantee and is unit-testable with zero GPU involvement; pixel-level output is only a deterministic function of that recipe on a given device/OS, never claimed or tested as byte-identical across GPU families or OS revisions.
decisions.rationale: Core Image's GPU-backed rendering is not contractually byte-stable across GPU families/OS versions, so testing determinism by comparing exported PNG bytes across Simulator vs. device or across an OS update would produce false failures and misrepresent what's actually guaranteed.
rejected_alternatives: Testing/claiming determinism via byte-identical PNG comparison across environments
constraints: Recipe-struct equality is the CI-testable determinism contract; pixel comparison is only valid within a single process/environment

decisions.decision: SwiftData schema is defined via VersionedSchema/SchemaMigrationPlan starting at v1, even though only one schema version exists at ship.
decisions.rationale: This app has no server and no sync; the local store is the only copy of the user's history forever, so migration support must exist before it's needed rather than being retrofitted after a v2 schema change already requires it.
rejected_alternatives: Plain unversioned SwiftData model, adding migration support only when a schema change is actually needed
constraints: DayEntry/AuraCard and MonthlyWrapped models must be defined inside a VersionedSchema from the start

decisions.decision: The canonical 'last completed calendar day' value exposed by AuraStore must be derived live from a SwiftData query (max date of non-demo DayEntry records), never cached as a separate scalar in UserDefaults or elsewhere.
decisions.rationale: A cached scalar that can drift from the actual persisted records is the same single-source-of-truth failure mode this project has already caught itself on in other areas (day-state, widget reload, entitlement snapshot), just relocated.
rejected_alternatives: Caching the last-completed-day value separately in UserDefaults for quick access
constraints: Any read of 'today's lock state' must go through a query against persisted DayEntry records

decisions.decision: Standard iOS device/iTunes local backup of the SwiftData store is explicitly permitted and expected, and is distinct from the already-banned CloudKit-mirrored container.
decisions.rationale: These are different mechanisms; conflating ordinary device backup with the prohibited CloudKit sync would incorrectly imply the app needs to actively defeat standard iOS backup behavior.
rejected_alternatives: Treating standard device backup as equivalent to the banned CloudKit sync and disabling/excluding the store from backup

decisions.decision: No location, camera, microphone, health, or contacts access anywhere in the app; export uses ShareLink(item:) with a Transferable image rather than a hand-rolled UIActivityViewController; there is no direct Photos-library write affordance, so no NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription or any other privacy-related Info.plist usage-description key is required.
decisions.rationale: Keeping export strictly share-sheet-based removes an entire permission-denial state (Photos write access) that would otherwise need its own design and test coverage, and matches the app's overall minimal-permissions posture.
rejected_alternatives: Adding a direct 'Save to Photos' button requiring NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription
Hand-rolling UIActivityViewController instead of using SwiftUI's native ShareLink
constraints: If a direct Photos-save feature is ever added later, it must add its own permission state and Info.plist key at that time

decisions.decision: StoreKitTest/SKTestSession is added as the automated-regression test backbone for purchase, restore, and regeneration-entitlement logic, run in a normal XCTest target, alongside (not instead of) manual .storekit-configuration testing in Simulator for the human-eyeballed paywall/purchase-sheet UX pass.
decisions.rationale: Manual Simulator testing with a .storekit file proves the UI flow works but isn't repeatable by CI or a fast test suite; StoreKitTest can script real Transaction flows including refunds in a normal test target, giving repeatable coverage on the riskiest must-have without overclaiming what Simulator alone can prove for real transaction completion.
rejected_alternatives: Relying solely on manual .storekit Simulator testing with no automated StoreKit test coverage
constraints: StoreKitTest coverage and manual Simulator UX testing are complementary and both required, not either/or

decisions.decision: BGTaskScheduler and any background-execution primitive are explicitly ruled out; monthly Wrapped generation and widget staleness are computed lazily on next foreground (scenePhase == .active check for 'has the calendar month rolled over') and via the widget's own timeline provider reading the shared App Group cache.
decisions.rationale: There's no server push and no reason to wake the app in the background; foreground-lazy computation has no background-execution budget to fight and can't silently fail to run the way a BGAppRefreshTask can.
rejected_alternatives: Using BGAppRefreshTask/BGTaskScheduler to precompute Wrapped or refresh the widget in the background
constraints: Wrapped/month-rollover checks must be tied to scenePhase transitions or the widget timeline provider, not a background task

decisions.decision: The 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (DEC-prompt_contract-003) is implemented as a concrete architectural deliverable: a debug-only render harness (Xcode Previews or a debug menu screen, stripped from Release builds) that batch-renders a fixed, checked-in set of canonical seed/mood/chip combinations and displays/writes them for side-by-side review; the same harness is reused to validate demo-vs-real visual parity (DEC-per_app_product_brief-007) by rendering both demo-seeded and fresh-input cards through the identical pipeline.
decisions.rationale: A one-time manual 'someone eyeballs the Simulator' pass is not a reliable enough mechanism to survive a real build under time pressure; making it a rerunnable, checked-in artifact turns the beauty gate and the demo-parity check into something any reviewer can regenerate and inspect in thirty seconds.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the visual-review checkpoint as a one-time manual pass with no persistent harness or artifact
constraints: Harness must be excluded from Release builds
Harness must render both demo-seeded and fresh-input cards for the parity check, not just the base 8-10+ combination set

decisions.decision: No CoreML, ARKit, or on-device ML of any kind is used anywhere in the app; restated here as an explicit won't-build guardrail rather than an unstated absence.
decisions.rationale: The app's caption and mood-mapping promise is 'deterministic, curated, never hallucinated' — any future temptation to swap in an ML classifier for 'smarter' mood inference would directly break that promise.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving ML/AR exclusion implicit rather than stating it as a guardrail
constraints: Any future ML/AR proposal must be treated as a scope change requiring its own justification, not a quiet addition

decisions.decision: Mood vocabulary is fixed at 8 values (Radiant, Calm, Wistful, Restless, Tender, Fierce, Hazy, Hopeful) arranged as a radial wheel for coherent hue-rotation palette mapping.
decisions.rationale: Unblocks the 8-10+ combination visual-review checkpoint (already dependent on this per DEC-detailed_discussion-010) and gives palette derivation a structured basis instead of an arbitrary list.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving mood count/ordering unspecified until build time
constraints: Palette-mapping logic in the renderer must use the wheel ordering, not treat moods as an unordered enum

decisions.decision: Chip vocabulary is fixed at 24 values across 4 families of 6 (texture, weather, pace, company); user selects 1-2 per check-in.
decisions.rationale: Produces 2,400 mood/chip combinations before the date seed is even applied, giving the seed-space enough richness to make 'meaningfully different days' true by construction.
rejected_alternatives: A smaller flat chip list with no family structure
constraints: Family grouping affects curation/UI grouping only, never selection or seeding logic

decisions.decision: The generative algorithm hashes (dateKey, moodID, sorted chipIDs, timeOfDayBucket, entitlementSnapshot, regenerationNonce) via SHA256 into a splitmix64 stream, and drives composition through a small deterministic pure-Swift noise implementation (continuous flow-field), not a fixed set of recolored templates.
decisions.rationale: A template-plus-recolor approach is exactly the failure mode the prompt calls out ('same template recolored'); a continuous noise-driven field makes structural variation, not just hue variation, the default outcome.
rejected_alternatives: Picking from a small library of fixed shape-field templates and recoloring per seed
constraints: Debug render harness must include adjacent-seed pairs (same mood, consecutive dates) to catch noise-field degeneracy (banding, near-identical adjacent fields) before ship

decisions.decision: Captions are composed from 3 independently-tracked fragment pools (opener / mood-core / chip-inflected closer), each with its own 30-day no-repeat window, rather than one flat curated phrase bank per mood.
decisions.rationale: A flat bank can't realistically survive a user who picks the same mood and regenerates daily (up to 60 draws against one mood's pool in 30 days) without heavy curation; combinatorial fragment composition makes exhaustion structurally near-impossible from a modest curated set.
rejected_alternatives: One flat per-mood phrase bank sized to avoid 30-day repeats
constraints: Each fragment slot's no-repeat window is tracked independently via CaptionEligibilityQuery

decisions.decision: Models, Engine (seed hash/noise/palette/caption selection), and Persistence are pulled into a local Swift Package (AuraKit, file:// reference) linked identically by the app target, the widget extension, and the test target.
decisions.rationale: The widget needs CachedCardMetadata decoding and the test target needs the GPU-free recipe engine (per the recipe/pixel determinism split); a local package guarantees one compiled source instead of the same .swift file added to multiple targets and silently drifting, the same two-sources-of-truth shape this project has flagged repeatedly elsewhere.
rejected_alternatives: Adding shared .swift files directly to multiple target memberships
constraints: AuraKit must have zero UIKit/SwiftUI/CoreImage imports; rendering stays in the app target

decisions.decision: Date/timezone access is abstracted behind an AuraClock protocol (now(), currentTimeZone()), with SystemClock live and TestClock for XCTest, injected into AuraStore and DayStateResolver.
decisions.rationale: Lets the already-locked DST/backward-clock/date-line rules get fast, deterministic, CI-runnable unit tests instead of relying solely on a human manually flipping the Simulator's clock.
rejected_alternatives: Reading Date()/TimeZone.current directly inside AuraStore/DayStateResolver
constraints: Manual Simulator date/timezone changes remain the acceptance-level check per the decision log; TestClock is additive, not a replacement

decisions.decision: The main SwiftData ModelContainer lives in the app's default private container; only rendered PNGs (full-res, thumbnail, bloom intermediates) and CachedCardMetadata are written into the App Group shared container for the widget.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the single source of truth (SwiftData store) in the app's own sandbox while giving the widget exactly what it needs (per DEC-design_handoff-003) without exposing ModelContext across the process boundary.
rejected_alternatives: Placing the entire SwiftData store inside the App Group container
constraints: Widget extension never links against or opens the app's ModelContainer directly

decisions.decision: The debug render harness (already mandated by DEC-ios_architecture_review-009) must include adjacent-seed pairs (same mood, consecutive dates) in its canonical combination set, not just diverse combinations.
decisions.rationale: A buggy noise implementation could produce collapsed/near-identical output for adjacent seeds without producing an obviously broken single render; only an adjacent-pair comparison would catch that specific failure mode.
rejected_alternatives: Only including maximally diverse combinations in the harness's canonical set
constraints: Must be checked in as part of the harness's fixed combination list, not left to ad hoc manual selection

decisions.decision: Regeneration divergence is enforced algebraically via RegenerationDivergenceEngine.perturb — nonzero modular offset on palette index, nonzero XOR mask on the flow-field seed — rather than left to hash-stream probability.
decisions.rationale: A shared hash-stream draw only makes divergence likely, not guaranteed; at real usage scale a coincidental collision on 2+ fields would silently ship a regenerate button that does nothing for some users, directly violating DEC-per_app_product_brief-002.
rejected_alternatives: Drawing regenerated fields from the same hash stream with a different nonce and relying on statistical likelihood of divergence
constraints: Must be provable via one deterministic unit test (e.g. 500 seed triples, assert >=2-of-3 field divergence, zero flake) rather than a statistical/repeated-run test

decisions.decision: CompositionFamily (paintBloom, particleField, flowLines) is a first-class recipe field mapping directly to the three visual languages named in the original prompt; the base recipe draws it from its own hash lane, and regeneration forces a different family via the same nonzero-offset mechanism as palette/topology.
decisions.rationale: Without this, the engine would only ever produce one continuous noise-driven visual language regardless of what the prompt promised, and a paid regeneration would only ever be a numeric shift rather than a genuinely different kind of picture.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all three named visual languages as flavor text and building only one continuous parameterized noise field
constraints: If build bandwidth is insufficient to render all 3 families at full quality, cut to 2 families (paintBloom plus one of particleField/flowLines) rather than ship a third at lower quality — beauty bar takes priority over family count

decisions.decision: Palette library is fixed at 32 total curated palettes; free tier resolves paletteIndex mod 16 (first 16), Aura+ resolves mod 32 (full library), via PaletteLibrary.paletteCount(for:)/resolvePalette(index:tier:).
decisions.rationale: Makes the 'expanded palette library' Aura+ unlock a pure function of the already-snapshotted entitlement rather than a separate runtime toggle, keeping it consistent with the no-retroactive-mutation rule (DEC-detailed_discussion-011).
rejected_alternatives: A separate settings-driven palette-unlock flag independent of the entitlement snapshot
constraints: Palette resolution must read from the EntitlementSnapshot stored on the DayEntry at generation time, never current live entitlement

decisions.decision: Demo history's anchor date range is computed exactly once, on first demo-mode enable (34-day range ending 1 day before the earliest real DayEntry, or today if none exists), and persisted via DemoAnchorStore; every later render reads the persisted range rather than recomputing.
decisions.rationale: A range recomputed from 'now' on every enable would drift and could eventually collide with real usage dates after enough toggling over a long enough time; computing and freezing it once makes collision structurally impossible permanently, not just today.
rejected_alternatives: Recomputing the anchor range relative to 'now' each time demo mode is toggled on
constraints: 34-day range comfortably exceeds the 30+ day demo history requirement (DEC-product_research-005)

decisions.decision: MoodTrendAggregator.chartData(entries:range:granularity:) returns [MoodTrendDataPoint] (bucketDate, mood, count) directly consumable by Swift Charts BarMark; demo-flagged entries participate in the aggregate identically to real entries, with no separate exclusion logic since the demo/real distinction is already handled visually at the archive-badge/banner level.
decisions.rationale: Turns a vague 'aggregation function' into a concrete, chart-ready contract, and avoids inventing a second demo-labeling mechanism when the archive's per-cell badge already satisfies the non-empty-and-honest requirement for trend data.
rejected_alternatives: A generic dictionary/tuple aggregation function requiring the UI layer to reshape it for Charts
Excluding demo entries from the trend aggregate by default
constraints: Weekly granularity is the default for the roughly-30-day window used by both real and demo history

decisions.decision: AuraRenderer.renderBloomIntermediates must return exactly 4 CIImages for every CompositionFamily; family-specific rendering differences happen inside each of the 4 stages (wash/shape-field/density/color-grade), never by changing the number of stages or the 3-haptic-beat timing already locked in DEC-design_handoff-004.
decisions.rationale: Introducing 3 composition families this phase creates a real risk of silently breaking the already-locked bloom-reveal choreography if particleField or flowLines end up needing a structurally different rendering pipeline; stating this as an explicit constraint prevents that from being discovered as a bug during build.
rejected_alternatives: Letting each composition family define its own number of reveal stages/haptic beats
constraints: Applies to all 3 families uniformly; any family whose natural rendering process doesn't fit 4 discrete stages must be adapted to fit, not exempted

decisions.decision: If time pressure forces a cut to the composition-family scope, the mandated fallback is to ship 2 well-built families (paintBloom plus one of particleField/flowLines) rather than 3 families at reduced quality.
decisions.rationale: Restates the round-2 contributor's explicit risk mitigation as a binding build-phase decision, since 'beauty is the single most important requirement' means a mediocre third visual language actively hurts the app more than a missing one.
rejected_alternatives: Forcing all 3 families through at whatever quality time allows
constraints: This is a scope-cut fallback only, not a default target — build should attempt all 3 families first

decisions.decision: AuraKit (models, AuraRecipe, SeedEngine, RegenerationDivergenceEngine, DayStateResolver, VersionedSchema/SchemaMigrationPlan, AuraClock/TestClock, CaptionEligibilityQuery) is a hard-blocking first milestone, fully built and unit-tested before any SwiftUI screen is built against it.
decisions.rationale: Every screen state across Today/Archive/Wrapped is defined in terms of values this layer produces; discovering a recipe or entitlement-shape mistake after UI is already built against it means rework, not iteration.
rejected_alternatives: Sequencing by the must/should/could feature priority list (check-in UI, then archive, then Wrapped, then StoreKit, then widget) instead of by actual dependency graph
constraints: No UI work should be scheduled to start before AuraKit's determinism/regeneration/day-state test suite is green

decisions.decision: The renderer (CIContext pipeline, 3 composition families) is treated as the plan's largest unknown and critical path, with an explicit build-and-check checkpoint: build paintBloom fully end-to-end through the debug render harness before starting particleField or flowLines, and make a real go/no-go call at that checkpoint rather than discovering the need to cut scope at ship time.
decisions.rationale: Aesthetic iteration on three genuinely distinct, beautiful rendering pipelines has no time estimate anywhere upstream and is exactly the kind of work that blows through estimates; the already-agreed 2-family fallback (DEC-tech_specs-015) only works if something concrete forces the decision point to actually happen.
rejected_alternatives: Treating the 3-families-vs-2 fallback as self-triggering prose with no scheduled checkpoint
constraints: Debug render harness must exist and be usable the moment paintBloom's first intermediate renders, not after all families are nominally done

decisions.decision: EntitlementSnapshot's data shape and a deterministic test/fake entitlement provider (defaulting to free tier) must exist from the first day AuraKit development starts, even though the actual StoreKitManager purchase-sheet UI wiring can be sequenced later.
decisions.rationale: EntitlementSnapshot is baked into AuraRecipe/DayEntry from the very first generated card; without an explicit test fixture, early development risks an ad hoc placeholder entitlement value that never gets consistently replaced or gets hardcoded to isAuraPlus:true for developer convenience and quietly ships.
