rejected_alternatives: Deferring all entitlement-related work, including the data shape, until StoreKit integration is scheduled near the end
constraints: A free-tier-default entitlement test fixture must be part of AuraKit's initial deliverable, not added later

decisions.decision: The AuraRenderer protocol (declared in terms of CIImage/CGImage) must live in the app target, not inside the AuraKit package, since AuraKit is contractually zero-CoreImage/UIKit.
decisions.rationale: If task assignment interprets 'Engine' as including the renderer protocol, it either violates AuraKit's zero-CoreImage constraint or forces a later module-boundary redo.
rejected_alternatives: Placing the renderer protocol inside AuraKit alongside the other engine types since it feels conceptually similar
constraints: AuraKit exports only pure AuraRecipe/AuraStore-facing types; the renderer protocol and its implementation stay in the app target

decisions.decision: Verification work is split by nature, not scheduled as one end-of-plan phase: GPU-free tests (recipe determinism, the 500-seed regeneration-divergence test, DayStateResolver behavior under TestClock for DST/backward-clock/date-line) are written test-first as part of the AuraKit milestone itself; render- and device-dependent checks (8-10+ combination visual review, demo-vs-real parity, manual Simulator date/timezone manipulation, StoreKitTest flows, export pixel-dimension/EXIF checks) are scheduled as their own dedicated, time-budgeted late-stage milestone.
decisions.rationale: Folding all verification into 'final polish' risks the two checks that actually gate the app's stated primary goal (visual review, demo-vs-real parity) getting no real time budget; GPU-free tests are naturally part of building AuraKit correctly and shouldn't wait for a separate testing phase.
rejected_alternatives: Treating all verification, GPU-free and render-dependent alike, as a single testing phase at the end
constraints: Visual-review and demo-vs-real parity checks must have their own scheduled time, not be assumed to happen incidentally during other work

decisions.decision: Demo history generation (30+ varied, genuinely good cards via DemoAnchorStore) is a gating dependency for the Archive/Wrapped/Trend UI milestone, scheduled immediately after the renderer milestone closes, not batched into general UI/content polish.
decisions.rationale: Archive, trend, and Wrapped screens cannot be meaningfully built or reviewed without seeded history to look at, and generating 30+ good-looking varied cards is itself a real exercise of the rendering pipeline across many seed combinations, not incidental content work.
rejected_alternatives: Treating demo history as content work schedulable whenever convenient during UI polish
constraints: Demo history generation must be scheduled as its own step between the renderer milestone and the Archive/Wrapped/Trend UI milestone

decisions.decision: Widget and local notifications are identified as the one legitimate parallelization opportunity in the plan, buildable alongside Archive/Wrapped UI work once the renderer and App Group cache writer exist, since both surfaces primarily read CachedCardMetadata rather than depend on other UI screens.
decisions.rationale: Unlike AuraKit and the renderer, which are strictly sequential blockers for everything downstream, widget/notifications have a narrow, already-defined data dependency (CachedCardMetadata) that unblocks early relative to the rest of the UI.
rejected_alternatives: Treating widget/notifications as strictly sequential after all core UI is complete
constraints: Widget/notification work should only start once the App Group cache writer and its metadata format are stable

decisions.decision: A dedicated M0 scaffolding milestone precedes AuraKit work: app target, widget extension target, a test target linking AuraKit, App Group entitlement provisioned on both app and widget targets, a checked-in .storekit configuration file, and a stubbed Theme.swift.
decisions.rationale: Treating project/target/entitlement scaffolding as 'obviously implied' risks the same two-sources-of-truth drift this project has flagged repeatedly elsewhere, just relocated to the target-configuration level (e.g. AuraKit tests written against a package never actually wired into the real app/widget/test triad, or an unprovisioned App Group identifier discovered late).
rejected_alternatives: Treating scaffolding as an implicit, unscheduled prerequisite folded into the start of the AuraKit milestone
constraints: M0 must complete, including App Group provisioning on both app and widget targets, before M1 AuraKit work is considered started

decisions.decision: Content curation (24 chip names, 32 palette hex sets, the 3 caption fragment pools) is scoped inside M1 as real creative work with a hard cap at the already-specified counts, explicitly rejecting open-ended 'just a few more for variety' expansion.
decisions.rationale: Unbounded content curation is exactly the kind of task that silently expands and eats into the time budget the renderer milestone (M2) actually needs, which is the plan's real critical path.
rejected_alternatives: Treating content curation as open-ended polish schedulable at any point
constraints: Ship exactly 24 chips / 32 palettes / the specified caption fragment counts; no scope growth beyond spec

decisions.decision: The M2 renderer checkpoint from round 1 is given a concrete operational trigger: build paintBloom fully (all 4 stages, thumbnail, export, Wrapped poster variant) and pass it through the debug harness first; then run one bounded iteration pass on particleField and evaluate, across at least 3 canonical seeds, whether it reads as structurally different from paintBloom (not just recolored); keep and repeat for flowLines only if yes, cut immediately per the existing 2-family fallback if no.
decisions.rationale: A checkpoint without a concrete pass/fail question is not a real decision point — this converts 'cut under time pressure' from a decision nobody wants to make in the moment into one the plan has already pre-committed to.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the checkpoint as a general 'review quality and decide' step with no concrete test
constraints: The structural-difference question must be evaluated against at least 3 of the harness's canonical seeds before deciding to keep or cut a family

decisions.decision: The debug render harness must write its canonical renders to a fixed, inspectable location on disk (not only an ephemeral Xcode Previews canvas), and the milestone step that closes out the visual-beauty gate must include a documented action of actually opening and inspecting a sample of those files, not merely confirming the harness ran without crashing.
decisions.rationale: Given this project's build process is itself running autonomously (repeated 'Run autonomous app orchestration' commits with no human-authored commits between), 'the harness executed successfully' would otherwise silently substitute for the actual human/model visual judgment every prior phase has required — precisely the failure mode portfolio_selection named as the one to guard against.
rejected_alternatives: Treating harness execution without a crash as sufficient evidence the beauty gate was satisfied
constraints: Applies to both M2's family-checkpoint and M7's formal 8-10+ combination visual-review pass

decisions.decision: M3 (demo history) bundles the demo-vs-real visual parity comparison (a handful of fresh cards vs. matching demo cards, compared side by side) into the same milestone as demo-history generation, rather than deferring it to end-stage verification.
decisions.rationale: The comparison is cheap to run the moment both demo and fresh generation paths exist, and expensive to discover as broken later once other work has been built on top of an assumption of parity.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring the demo-vs-real parity check entirely to the final verification milestone
constraints: Parity check must be run as part of M3's close-out, not solely at M7

decisions.decision: M4 (Today check-in/reveal flow) must be built and tested against real rendered output from M2/M3, never placeholder gradients standing in for 'the renderer isn't done yet' — with the caption-legibility contrast fallback specifically named as needing a real busy/unpredictable composition to test against, not a mocked pastel gradient.
decisions.rationale: Building UI in parallel against fake images to save time either never exercises the 4.5:1 contrast fallback for real or gives it a false sense of confidence from unrepresentative test images.
rejected_alternatives: Starting M4 UI work in parallel with M2 using placeholder images to save time
constraints: M4 cannot start meaningfully until M2 has produced real renderable output for at least the surviving composition family/families

decisions.decision: M5 (Archive/Trend/Wrapped UI) and M6 (StoreKit + Widget + Notifications, as three sub-lanes within one milestone rather than three separate milestones) run as parallel lanes once M1's entitlement plumbing and M2's App Group cache writer exist.
decisions.rationale: M6's three surfaces share the same 'should-have, riskiest-must-have-adjacent' framing from app_features, depend only on already-completed foundational work, and don't block each other, making this the one legitimate fork in an otherwise strictly sequential dependency graph.
rejected_alternatives: Treating StoreKit, widget, and notifications as three independent milestones
Sequencing M5 and M6 one after the other instead of in parallel
constraints: M6 must not start before the App Group cache writer format is stable

decisions.decision: M7 is a single named, time-budgeted final verification milestone covering the formal 8-10+ combination visual review, demo-vs-real parity confirmation, the manual Simulator date/timezone/DST/backward-clock/date-line pass, StoreKitTest's scripted purchase/refund/restore suite, export dimension/EXIF/watermark-placement checks, dark mode/accessibility passes, and the entitlement non-retroactive-mutation check (buy Aura+ mid-sequence, confirm earlier cards unchanged) — not a generic end-of-plan 'verify everything' paragraph.
decisions.rationale: These are the literal, already-accumulated acceptance criteria from nine prior phases; treating them as an afterthought risks exactly the 'renders without crashing' rubber-stamp failure mode this project has repeatedly warned against.
rejected_alternatives: Distributing these checks informally across other milestones with no dedicated budgeted time
Treating verification as unscheduled polish at the very end
constraints: Each listed check must be present as its own line item in M7 with a concrete reviewer-executable action, per DEC-app_features-007

decisions.decision: Lane ownership follows tech_specs' existing owning_lane tags rather than a fresh split: data_domain owns the AuraKit package; services_utilities owns AuraClock/DayStateResolver and the entire renderer (protocol, CIContext pipeline, all 3 composition families, debug harness); primary_ui owns AuraStore, routing, Theme.swift, and every screen/component; polish_resilience owns StoreKit, widget, notifications, export, accessibility descriptions, and M7 verification.
decisions.rationale: This mapping was already thought through and locked in tech_specs' interfaces-json; inventing a new split (e.g. per-screen) would cut across already-agreed module boundaries.
rejected_alternatives: A feature-based split (one lane per screen/feature) independent of tech_specs' owning_lane tags
constraints: The renderer stays under services_utilities even though it feels UI-adjacent, specifically to prevent a second rendering path forming under primary_ui

decisions.decision: Forbidden edit zones are locked: AuraKit/Sources is data_domain-only, Theme.swift and AuraStore.swift are primary_ui-only, and project.pbxproj is never hand-edited as raw text (only through Xcode's add-file flow).
decisions.rationale: These are the specific files where cross-lane drive-by edits would recreate the two-sources-of-truth bug this project has flagged repeatedly (day-state, widget reload, entitlement snapshot) at the file-ownership level instead.
rejected_alternatives: Allowing any lane to edit AuraKit or AuraStore directly when convenient
constraints: Cross-lane changes to these files must be requested of the owning lane, never applied directly

decisions.decision: Merge strategy is one branch per lane, cut only after that lane's hard dependency has merged to main; M0 scaffolding must fully merge before any other lane starts.
decisions.rationale: Preserves project_plan's M0->M1->M2->... sequencing (AuraKit before renderer, renderer's real output before Today UI) without needing complex locking — non-overlapping file ownership plus dependency-gated branch order is what actually prevents conflicts here.
rejected_alternatives: All four lanes starting in parallel from day one
constraints: services_utilities cannot start consuming AuraRecipe until data_domain's AuraKit test suite is green and merged; primary_ui's Today-flow work cannot start until services_utilities produces real rendered output

decisions.decision: Testing responsibility is split per lane rather than centralized: data_domain owns GPU-free AuraKit tests as part of its own deliverable; services_utilities owns the debug harness and the paintBloom-first go/no-go call; primary_ui owns manual walk-throughs of all six Today states and the Reduce Motion fallback; polish_resilience owns the M7 milestone, including the mandatory 'opened and inspected the on-disk harness files' documented action rather than 'the harness ran.'
decisions.rationale: Operationalizes project_plan's verification split and its specific fix for an autonomous build pipeline, where 'executed without crashing' could otherwise silently substitute for real visual judgment.
rejected_alternatives: A single end-of-build QA pass owning all testing
constraints: M7 sign-off docs must state what was actually opened and looked at, not just that a script ran

decisions.decision: A canonical accessibilityIdentifier map is locked for every control referenced by the flows-json UI-crawl contract (tab bar, check-in flow, share/regenerate, archive grid/trend, Wrapped poster, Settings/StoreKit rows), and folded into the acceptance criteria of the task that owns each control's file.
decisions.rationale: The UI-crawl gate matches on the literal identifier string; a drifted or missing identifier fails the gate even if the underlying feature works correctly.
rejected_alternatives: Relying on matching visible labels, which drift as copy gets polished during build
constraints: Identifiers are dotted screen.controlName strings; chip identifiers are index-based (today.wordChip.N) since exact chip copy isn't fixed by this phase

decisions.decision: AuraTabBar and AuraTopBar — named in design_handoff's component inventory but absent from the initial task backlog — are added as an explicit new task (T-041) owned by primary_ui.
decisions.rationale: These are load-bearing design requirements (explicitly rejecting stock tab bar material and default large-title nav) and were the one real gap found while finalizing this phase's task list; leaving them implicit risked them being built as an afterthought or with stock chrome.
rejected_alternatives: Assuming the tab bar/top bar would get built incidentally as part of other screen tasks
constraints: T-041 must not use stock translucent tab bar material or default large-title NavigationStack chrome

decisions.decision: flows-json declares 7 fully self-contained journeys (each assumes a fresh app launch rather than chaining off another flow's end state) covering check-in+reveal+share, demo-seeded archive browsing, the trend chart, Wrapped, Aura+ purchase, honest restore, and purchase+regenerate.
decisions.rationale: Matches the phase's required 3-8 flow coverage of every primary promise while staying safe against an unknown flow-runner state model between separate flow invocations.
rejected_alternatives: Chaining flows that assume state left behind by a previous flow (e.g. assuming check-in already happened before testing share)
constraints: Any flow needing a completed check-in re-performs the check-in steps itself rather than assuming prior state

decisions.decision: Build is cleared to start; the plan is internally consistent across all ten prior phases with no contradictions requiring scope downgrade.
decisions.rationale: Requirement-to-task mapping is complete, lane/file ownership matches tech_specs' own assignments, every primary user promise has a UI-crawl flow, and the highest-risk items (visual beauty, determinism, regeneration divergence, entitlement immutability) all have concrete, reviewer-executable tests rather than prose assurances.
rejected_alternatives: Holding the gate open pending a Codex adversarial pass that has been unavailable since detailed_discussion round 1
constraints: The three amendments below (DEC-002, DEC-003, DEC-004) must be folded into the task backlog before the affected tasks (WrappedAggregator, T-024, T-016/T-017) are picked up

decisions.decision: A new data_domain task, WrappedAggregator (mirroring MoodTrendAggregator's shape: pure function, testable, no UI dependency), is added to compute a month's or partial-history's dominant palette/mood story for the Wrapped poster; if cut for time, the poster must fall back to displaying the single most recent qualifying card, never a fabricated narrative or a broken/empty screen.
decisions.rationale: The existing backlog wired the Wrapped poster's rendering and UI shell (T-018, T-029) but never specified what computes the actual recap content from underlying DayEntry records — leaving this unstated would force whoever builds T-029 to invent the aggregation logic mid-build, the exact kind of decision this gate exists to prevent.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving Wrapped's content-aggregation logic unspecified and trusting the build lane to invent something reasonable
Treating T-018's renderer reuse as sufficient without a data-aggregation task
constraints: Owned by data_domain, consumed by primary_ui's T-029
Must have a named, explicit fallback (most-recent-qualifying-card) if not built, since Wrapped remains should-have

decisions.decision: The mood-vocabulary's radial-wheel ordering (tech_specs) governs internal MoodID enum adjacency for palette hue-rotation continuity only; the rendered MoodChipCluster picker must be a tappable grid/cluster of large-hit-target icon+label shapes, never a literal spinning dial control.
decisions.rationale: A literal radial/dial UI widget is a fussier, small-angular-target interaction pattern that directly conflicts with the app's own sub-10-second, half-asleep, one-thumb check-in promise restated as a hard acceptance bar since initial_discussion; design_handoff and design_discussion already named the component 'MoodChipCluster' and 'tactile icon+label shapes,' but the tech_specs wheel language is ambiguous enough to be misread as a literal UI directive under build time pressure.
rejected_alternatives: Leaving the wheel-ordering language as-is and trusting the build lane to correctly infer it's a data-model concern only
constraints: Applies to T-024 (MoodChipCluster + WordChipCluster component task) as an added acceptance-criteria constraint

decisions.decision: The particleField and flowLines composition-family go/no-go checkpoints (T-016, T-017) are bounded to exactly one implementation pass plus at most one revision pass per family before the structural-difference pass/cut decision must fire, with no further iteration permitted.
decisions.rationale: project_plan's 'one bounded iteration pass' had no concrete numeric bound, which is fine for a human making a live judgment call but risky in an autonomous pipeline with no one in the loop between orchestration runs — it could get rubber-stamped on the first attempt (defeating the checkpoint's purpose) or spiral indefinitely chasing an ever-elusive 'good enough.'
rejected_alternatives: Leaving 'bounded iteration pass' undefined and trusting the build lane to stop at a reasonable point
Allowing unlimited revision passes until quality is judged sufficient
constraints: Applies to T-016 and T-017's acceptance criteria as an added numeric bound
The existing 2-family fallback (paintBloom + one of particleField/flowLines) remains the mandated outcome if either family fails its bounded checkpoint

decisions.decision: The manual QA checklist is split into two explicit tiers — Tier 1 (executable today against the current build) and Tier 2 (specified acceptance actions blocked on the unbuilt generative engine, DayStateResolver, and SwiftData persistence) — rather than one flat list.
decisions.rationale: Given build_verification confirmed the three hardest, most-decided requirements are still bootstrap stubs and the test target currently fails to compile, a single undifferentiated checklist would read as thorough while silently rubber-stamping stub code as tested — the exact failure mode named since portfolio_selection.
rejected_alternatives: Writing one flat checklist that treats all specified workflows as currently walkable
Omitting the blocked workflows entirely since they can't be run
constraints: Tier 2 items must preserve the exact, already-locked acceptance action (e.g. 'change Simulator date across a DST transition') so they aren't reinvented once the engine is built
No Tier 2 item may be reported as passed/checked until the underlying feature exists

decisions.decision: Every StoreKit-related checklist step must carry its Simulator-limitation caveat inline (proves initiation and local .storekit config only, never a completed real transaction), not as a single footnote.
decisions.rationale: Restates DEC-prompt_contract-008 concretely at the checklist level — burying the caveat once at the top risks individual purchase steps being read as fully verified in isolation.
rejected_alternatives: Stating the Simulator limitation once at the top of the StoreKit section only
constraints: Applies to purchase, restore, and any future refund-flow checklist steps

decisions.decision: Tier 1 is scoped to what the current shell actually supports: navigation/tab bar chrome, dark mode token application, Dynamic Type/VoiceOver on existing static content, notification permission paths, StoreKit purchase-sheet initiation, airplane-mode no-network verification, and force-quit/rotation crash safety.
decisions.rationale: These are the only workflows with real, non-stub code behind them right now; testing beyond this against stub logic (e.g. walking the check-in flow) would produce a false-positive pass on code that admittedly isn't the real implementation.
rejected_alternatives: Including check-in/reveal/archive/export as Tier 1 items with a caveat, rather than moving them to Tier 2 entirely
constraints: Tier 1 must be re-run once each blocked feature ships, since today's 'no crash on force-quit' baseline will need re-verification against real persisted state

decisions.decision: Launch readiness verdict is explicitly NOT READY: this phase's material is prepared as pre-drafted launch collateral, not a signal of shipping proximity, given the generative engine, DayStateResolver, and SwiftData persistence remain bootstrap stubs and the test target doesn't compile.
decisions.rationale: build_verification and human_qa_checklist already established the app's core promise is unbuilt; polished launch copy sitting next to a broken build would create a false impression of nearness, the exact risk this project has guarded against since portfolio_selection.
rejected_alternatives: Presenting launch material as if the app were near-ready since the paperwork itself is complete
constraints: Later phases must not treat a complete App Store readiness package as evidence the app is shippable

decisions.decision: Privacy nutrition label is locked as 'Data Not Collected' across every category, backed by the existing no-network/no-accounts/no-analytics/no-CloudKit architecture; a privacy policy URL and support URL must exist as real reachable pages before submission.
decisions.rationale: The architecture already guarantees this label's accuracy at zero marginal engineering cost; the URLs are a real, cheap, but genuine submission blocker if left until the last minute.
rejected_alternatives: Deferring privacy label/URL prep until the engine is built
constraints: Any future addition of a crash reporter or analytics SDK invalidates this label and must trigger a re-review of it

decisions.decision: Permission copy is scoped to exactly one system prompt (local notifications), with contextual (not cold-launch) soft-ask copy and a mandatory Settings.app deep-link on denial.
decisions.rationale: The architecture deliberately avoided any other permission-gated API (ShareLink instead of Photos write, no location/camera/mic/health/contacts), so this is the only permission surface that exists or needs review-facing copy.
rejected_alternatives: Drafting permission copy for hypothetical future permissions not in current scope
constraints: Denial path must route to Settings.app, not a dead in-app toggle

decisions.decision: Aura+ is submitted as a non-consumable (not subscription) with paywall copy required to describe exactly the three already-locked unlocks (watermark-free export, expanded palettes, daily regeneration); this cannot be finalized against real functional behavior until the entitlement/recipe pipeline is built, and IAP cannot be called verified until a sandbox-account pass runs on a physical device.
decisions.rationale: Guideline 3.1.2 risk comes from language implying recurring billing; the deeper risk is App Review functionally testing a purchase against paywall claims that nothing in the app currently performs, since entitlement snapshotting isn't wired to a real recipe yet.
rejected_alternatives: Treating Simulator-only StoreKit testing as sufficient verification for submission
constraints: Paywall functional claims must be re-validated once the entitlement/recipe pipeline is real, not assumed correct from design-phase intent

decisions.decision: The five-shot screenshot/storyboard plan (bloom reveal → archive grid → trend chart → Wrapped poster → Aura+ paywall) is fully specified but explicitly not executable until the renderer, persistence, and demo history exist; no placeholder/mockup capture is permitted as a substitute.
decisions.rationale: This project has already ruled out presenting placeholder content as real product screenshots; capturing against a UI-only build would produce screenshots that misrepresent the shipping app.
rejected_alternatives: Capturing screenshots now against a temporary/mocked UI to have something ready early
constraints: Screenshot capture must wait for real rendered output from the finished engine and real generated demo history

decisions.decision: Final verdict is NO-GO: Aura is not launch-ready and does not yet fulfill its stated core promise, despite compiling cleanly for the Simulator.
